sql: WITH populares AS (SELECT product_name, SUM(quantity) AS unidades_vendidas FROM v_order_lines WHERE order_status = 4 GROUP BY product_name ORDER BY unidades_vendidas DESC LIMIT 20), stock_tienda AS (SELECT p.product_name, st.store_id, SUM(st.quantity) AS stock FROM stocks st JOIN products p ON p.product_id = st.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name, st.store_id) SELECT pop.product_name AS producto, pop.unidades_vendidas, s.store_name AS tienda, sk.stock FROM populares pop JOIN stock_tienda sk ON sk.product_name = pop.product_name JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = sk.store_id WHERE sk.stock > 20 ORDER BY sk.stock DESC, pop.unidades_vendidas DESC
notas: Trampa: misma estructura que N2 pero el umbral va al revés (sobreinventario, no quiebre).

pregunta: ¿En qué ciudades se concentran las compras con el MAYOR descuento?
sql: WITH maximo AS (SELECT MAX(discount) AS d FROM order_items), general AS (SELECT customer_city, customer_state, AVG(discount) AS desc_prom, SUM(net_amount) AS ingreso_total FROM v_order_lines WHERE order_status = 4 GROUP BY customer_city, customer_state) SELECT l.customer_city AS ciudad, l.customer_state AS estado, ROUND(SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS ingreso_neto_desc_maximo, ROUND(100.0 * g.desc_prom, 2) AS descuento_promedio_pct, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(l.net_amount) / g.ingreso_total, 2) AS pct_ingreso_desc_maximo FROM v_order_lines l JOIN general g ON g.customer_city = l.customer_city AND g.customer_state = l.customer_state WHERE l.order_status = 4 AND l.discount = (SELECT d FROM maximo) GROUP BY l.customer_city, l.customer_state ORDER BY ingreso_neto_desc_maximo DESC LIMIT 10
